title: Clearwater Pond
briefing: Clearwater Pond used to be known for its stonewort meadows. Today the water is the colour of milky tea and the bed is bare. The parish council wants the underwater meadows back within three years. Plants need light at the bed, and many things in a shallow pond can steal it. Find out what is stealing it here before you spend the budget.

objective.text: Reach 30% submerged plant cover across Clearwater Pond by the end of year 3.

hints.text: Phosphorus in the pond is higher than the inflow can explain. Something inside the pond may be supplying it.
The new plantings are thinning out. What do they need that this water may not be giving them?
Carp numbers rarely stay low on their own. Where could new fish come from?
Most of the murk is sediment, not algae. Wind alone rarely keeps this much mud in suspension.

success_letter.address: The Village Hall, Mill Lane, Clearwater
paragraphs: On behalf of the Parish Council, and of everyone who walks the path around Clearwater Pond, thank you. Three years ago the water was the colour of milky tea. This summer the children on the jetty could see the bottom again.

Your final survey found {plant_cover} of the bed covered in submerged plants, against the {target} we had hoped for. The water now stays clear to a Secchi depth of {secchi}, and carp are down to {carp}.
We will admit that some of us expected you simply to plant the pond and go home. We are glad you looked closer first, and that you stopped the fish coming back up the inlet.
The stonewort meadows are back. Please come and see them. The Council would be pleased to welcome you at the summer fete, where the pond will be the first stop on the nature walk.
